objective: Let a mid-size SaaS company that builds features on third-party large language models decide which EU AI Act obligations it must meet, by when, and which points remain unsettled, so it can plan compliance work by date and know where to seek legal advice.

slots.name: company_role_under_act
slots.note: Building features on GPT/Claude implies the company is a downstream system provider and/or deployer, not a model provider.

slots.name: use_case_risk_tier
slots.note: Unspecified by the user; the answer must branch on it.

slots.name: modification_of_model
slots.type: whether the company fine-tunes or substantially modifies the model

constraints.text: Separate obligations already applicable on the as-of date from those that apply on later dates, with the date of each.
Identify points where experts, industry and regulators disagree or where guidance is pending.
Treat pending amendments (proposed delays or simplifications) as pending, not as law, unless adopted.
No legal advice framing: state what the sources say and where it is unsettled.

success_criteria.criterion: Every leaf sub-question in the cover has at least one finding.
Each application date the page states as settled rests on a verified finding (two or more independent publishers agree).
Every claim on the page traces to a source with a locator and a publisher.
Disagreements between sources are shown with both sides and their sources, no winner picked.
The page contains no internal method vocabulary.
The request and spec files validate against their formats.
